note: Views Google News is Views-only. It provides a style plugin google_news ('Google News Feed', display_types feed) and a row plugin google_news_fields ('Google News fields') that map view fields to Google News sitemap XML tags via row options loc_field / news_title_field / news_publication_date_field (required) and news_publication_name_field / news_publication_language_field / news_access_field / news_genres_field / news_keywords_field / news_stock_tickers_field. Name defaults to the site name, language to the default language. It also invokes hook_views_googlenews_item_alter(). No settings form, permissions, or drush. All cases are grounded in that real style/row config: introspection reads back the plugin ids / field mapping on a live view; execution builds a Google News feed view or switches an existing feed display to the google_news format, verified against the live view config.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal 11 site with views_googlenews, how do I output a View of my articles as a Google News sitemap feed? Which Views display type and which format (style) do I use?
evals.expected_output: Add a Feed display to the view and set its Format (style) to 'Google News Feed' (plugin id google_news, which only works on feed displays), then set the row style to 'Google News fields'. Give the feed display a path (e.g. news.xml).

evals.prompt: With views_googlenews, which Views row plugin renders each item, and how do I map the article URL, title and publication date to the Google News XML tags?
evals.expected_output: Use the 'Google News fields' row plugin (google_news_fields). In its settings map view fields to the row options: loc_field -> <loc>, news_title_field -> <news:title>, news_publication_date_field -> <news:publication_date> (these three are required); optional ones include news_keywords_field, news_access_field, news_genres_field, news_stock_tickers_field.

evals.prompt: In a views_googlenews feed, if I don't map a field for the publication name (<news:name>) or the language (<news:language>), what values are used? And which Google-recommended filter should the view have?
evals.expected_output: The publication name defaults to the site name and the language to the site's default language. Google recommends limiting to the last two days: add a 'Content: Authored on' filter with operator 'is greater than or equal to' and value offset 'now -2 days'.

evals.prompt: This site has a View named vgn_probe with a Feed display that outputs a Google News feed. Inspect the live view configuration and state the machine id of the Views style plugin its feed display uses.
evals.expected_output: The feed display's style plugin id is google_news (display feed_1: display_options.style.type = google_news; its row is google_news_fields).

evals.prompt: In the vgn_probe View's Google News feed display on this site, which view field id is mapped to the Google News <loc> element (the loc_field row option)? Inspect the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: loc_field is mapped to view_node (display feed_1: display_options.row.options.loc_field = view_node).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a View with machine id vgn_news that has a Feed display rendering content as a Google News sitemap: the feed display must use the 'Google News Feed' style and the 'Google News fields' row. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A view config views.view.vgn_news exists with a feed display whose display_options.style.type = google_news and display_options.row.type = google_news_fields (map loc/title/publication_date fields in the row options).

evals.prompt: This site has a View vgn_switch whose Feed display currently uses the default RSS format. Reconfigure that feed display to output a Google News sitemap instead: use the views_googlenews 'Google News Feed' style and 'Google News fields' row. Apply the change live.
evals.expected_output: In views.view.vgn_switch the feed display's display_options.style.type becomes google_news and display_options.row.type becomes google_news_fields (with the loc/title/publication_date row options mapped).
